results.title: How increasing the significance level affects statistical power
results.content: # How increasing the significance level affects statistical power. Ever scratched your head over terms like **statistical significance** and **power** while sifting through data? The **significance level (α)** helps us control the chance of making a Type I error. As it turns out, **increasing α generally boosts power**, but it also raises the risk of more Type I errors (here's why). It's crucial to understand that **power and significance level are distinct** concepts. Power reflects the likelihood of finding a real effect, while α controls how often we might find a false one. ## The relationship between significance level and statistical power. So, how do **significance level (α)** and **statistical power** interact? Boosting α enhances power, meaning we're more likely to spot true effects. Tweaking the **significance level (α)** has real-world consequences for your statistical tests. **Lowering α decreases power**, making it tougher to reject the null hypothesis (here's why). On the flip side, **increasing α can boost power**, letting you detect smaller effects without upping your sample size. Efficient resource allocation hinges on this balance between α and power. By choosing the right significance level, you optimize your experiment to detect meaningful effects while keeping false positives in check. ## Strategies for balancing significance level and power in experiments. Finding the right balance between **significance level (α)** and **power** is crucial for effective experiments. **Decreasing α reduces power**, making it harder to reject the null hypothesis (here's why). Conversely, **increasing α boosts power but raises the risk of false positives** (power vs significance). They help you determine the optimal sample size and significance level for your desired power. By carefully weighing the trade-offs between α and power, you can design experiments that effectively detect true effects. **Understanding significance levels** and leveraging power analysis tools will help you make confident, data-driven decisions. Navigating the interplay between **significance level** and **statistical power** is all about balance. Understanding how adjusting α affects your ability to detect real effects—and the risks of false positives—is essential for designing effective experiments. Whether you're running medical trials or A/B testing with Statsig's powerful tools, being mindful of this balance ensures you make informed, data-driven decisions.
